title: Twin under-deck tuned mass damper on HSFG-clamped cross-beam
problem_restatement: Retrofit a lively 40 m footbridge at 1.9 Hz with under-deck damping to bring Class III crowd shake into Medium comfort with no deck change and weight inside 2 %.
mechanism_sentence: Bridge motion shakes two hanging weights that lag behind and turn shake into heat, cutting deck shake from 8.28 m/s2 to 0.67 m/s2 while weight travel of 49.4 mm stays inside an 80 mm gap.
decisive_choices: Twin 400 kg pair detuned about 1.83 Hz (C20) beats single exact absorber on robustness holding 0.476 to 0.526 m/s2 and beats stiffening needing 46.5 % more stiffness as impractical and beats no-means which sizes but supplies no force.

HSFG-clamped cross-beam carrying 7.85 kN plus 5.22 kN into girders as shear (C22) beats generic welded bracket on fatigue and install with 32.9 kN slip per bolt versus 13.1 kN demand and beats sizing-only clamp and pipe analogy lacking two-unit embodiment and beats no-means which transfers nothing.

Paired viscous dampers with tolerant band inside twin units (C21) beats single optimum dashpot needing exact tune at same 12.0 % optimum and beats add-on parallel fluid unit lacking MTMD robustness and beats crowd case which sizes 1.66 kN force but dissipates nothing, giving 6.20 % effective damping.
open_question: Will the after-build Class III crowd walk-through confirm 0.67 m/s2 Medium comfort and file the acceptance record?
transfer_line: Vibration: main girders -> transverse cross-beam -> twin masses | Measured: midspan accelerometer -> comfort band verdict

assumed_constraints.constraint: total added dead load under 2% of pedestrian live load
vertical comfort target maximum comfort below 0.5 m/s2, mean 0.5-1.0 m/s2, minimum 1.0-2.5 m/s2, unacceptable above 2.5 m/s2 per Human-Induced Vibration on Lightweight Footbridges — 2024
maintenance by Below Bridge Access Vehicle or girder-bay walkway with lockable deck hatch per CDOT inspection-access rule, plus annual TMD tuning check — deck kept clear during service

concept.working_principle: bridge motion drives the two masses where motion is largest and the clamped frame carries the push into the girders, with damping doing the work through effective damping

parts.name: transverse cross-beam
parts.function: carries two damper units and moves with antinode

parts.name: coil spring suspension
parts.function: converts bridge motion into relative travel

parts.name: HSFG clamp bolt set
parts.function: clamps cross-beam to girders by friction

parts.name: deck accelerometer array
parts.function: logs vertical acceleration for comfort verdict

fabrication_steps.description: Fabricate short transverse steel cross-beam first, because both damper units and clamp bolts fix to it
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted steel fabrication, 2.5 to 3.0 m transverse beam

fabrication_steps.description: Hang twin 400 kg masses on coil springs with parallel viscous dampers on the beam next, because tuning and stroke are set on the assembled unit
fabrication_steps.method: Tuned assembly, steel 2 x 400 kg masses on 105 kN per m springs with viscous dampers at 1.83 Hz

fabrication_steps.description: Fit caged elastomer stops with 80 mm gap and lockable service pins next, because stops must clear 49.4 mm stroke after masses are hung
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted elastomer-steel stops, 80 mm gap for 124 mm sag plus stroke envelope

fabrication_steps.description: Clamp the assembled beam between girder webs with HSFG bolts from below last, because clamp carries full weight plus dynamics plus stop hit
fabrication_steps.method: Preloaded HSFG M20 grade 10.9 bolts, 32.9 kN slip per bolt

risks.mitigation: twin units detuned about optimum hold 0.476 to 0.526 m/s2 plus annual tuning check from below

risks.risk: clamp slip or preload loss under dynamics plus stop hit
risks.mitigation: 32.9 kN slip per bolt exceeds 13.1 kN demand including 8.40 kN stop hit with annual re-torque and stop-into-beam check

novelty_claim: Twin detuned masses on a single HSFG-clamped transverse beam within girder depth with caged stops and from-below service proven by crowd acceptance run
